message.content: **Summary:** I researched Apple's latest results and news, then bought 40 shares of AAPL at a limit of $222.75 (filled at $222.75, ~$8,910 total — within the $10,000 per-order and $20,000 daily caps, and funded entirely from existing cash with no money moved out). Apple's fiscal Q4 2024 (quarter ended Sept 28, 2024) showed revenue of $94.9B, up 6% year over year, and the just-filed FY2024 10-K (filed 2024-11-01) reported total net sales of $391,035M, net income of $93,736M, diluted EPS of $6.08 (including a one-time $10.2B tax charge), and operating cash flow of $118,254M — a highly cash-generative business trading at roughly 36.6x trailing EPS. News flow was neutral-to-constructive: shares were steady around $222 as investors weighed iPhone 16 demand and the gradual Apple Intelligence rollout, and I treated a promotional "FY25 outlook" page claiming $9.50 EPS and >25% revenue growth as unverified marketing content rather than a company filing, so I did not rely on it. Given solid fundamentals, a modestly positive demand narrative, and a quote ($222.70 last, bid/ask $222.68/$222.72) essentially at market, I placed a single buy limit order at $222.75 — close to the current market price as the mandate requires — sized conservatively at about 45% of the per-order limit to leave room for a possible second order today.
